9	/-!
10	# THE `∀ T` BINDER OF THE `pic⁰` VANISHING IS A STATEMENT ABOUT TEST RINGS
11	
12	Two independent routes to a producer of `(pic0TypeFunctor C).RepresentableBy` meet at one
13	hypothesis, and that hypothesis has **no producer** anywhere in the project:
14	
15	  `hvan : ∀ S : Over (Spec k), Subsingleton (pic0Subgroup C S)`
16	
17	* `Pic0VanishingRoute.jacobianData_of_subsingleton` consumes it and returns a `JacobianData C`
18	  with no atlas, no chart certificate, no coverage and no divisor representability;
19	* `Pic0ChartSeamPairDecided.isLocallySurjective_abelSigmaChartZero_iff` proves the seam's
20	  *coverage* antecedent at parameter `0` is **equivalent** to it.
21	
22	So `hvan` is not one route's private input; it is where the two routes' costs coincide.
23	
24	**What this file does.** It replaces the `∀ T` quantifier — over all objects of
25	`Over (Spec k)`, i.e. over all `k`-schemes — by a quantifier over commutative `k`-algebras,
26	and it proves the replacement is an **equivalence**, not a sufficient condition.
27	
28	## Why the landed reduction does not already do this
29	
30	`Pic0VanishingRoute` reduces the quantifier for `picEt` (`subsingleton_picEt_of_affine`) and
31	proves that one is an equivalence (`subsingleton_picEtAff_of_forall`).  Its degree-zero
32	consequence `subsingleton_pic0_of_affine` runs **one way only**, and its own docstring says
33	why that is not a repair: the hypothesis is vanishing of the whole `picEt`, which is *strictly
34	stronger* and false at any curve carrying a class of nonzero degree — including `ℙ¹`, where
35	`pic⁰` does vanish.  So the landed chain cannot be applied to the hypothesis anyone needs, in
36	either direction.  The reduction here is for `pic0Subgroup` directly and never mentions
37	`picEt` vanishing.
38	
39	## The mechanism, and why it needed no new mathematics
40	
41	Separation, not gluing.  `Subsingleton` is an equality statement, so only the *ext* half of
42	the descent is used: the affine opens of `T.left` give a morphism-form open cover of `T` by
43	the affine-open test objects `Over.fromSpecAffine T U : overSpec k Γ(T.left, U) ⟶ T`
44	(`Picard/PicEtUnit.lean:60`), each an open immersion on the left because
45	`IsAffineOpen.fromSpec` is; and `pic0Subgroup_ext_of_cover`
46	(`Picard/PicEtCoverBridge.lean:342`) says two degree-zero classes agreeing on every member
47	agree.  Under the affine hypothesis each pair of restrictions agrees for free.
48	
49	The `∃!`-gluing bridge in the same file (`pic0Subgroup_existsUnique_of_cover`) is *not* used:
50	producing a class from local data would need the compatibility datum, and a subsingleton
51	statement never has to produce anything.  That asymmetry is the whole reason this is cheap
52	where the corresponding representability statement is not.
53	
54	## What the reduced hypothesis is, exactly
55	
56	Three equivalent spellings are given, each strictly more ring-level than the last:
57	
58	1. `Subsingleton (pic0Subgroup C (overSpec k A))` at every `k`-algebra `A` — the direct form;
59	2. the same transported through `picEtAffineEquiv` to a separation statement about **plus
60	   classes** `PicEtAff C A` of the test algebra, with the degree condition read through the
61	   comparison;
62	3. with the field points of `overSpec k A` themselves ring-level: every
63	   `t : overSpec k K ⟶ overSpec k A` **is** `Over.overSpecMap φ` for an algebra map
64	   `φ : A →ₐ[k] K` (`exists_algHom_eq_of_overSpec_hom`, `Spec.preimage` plus the tower

12	# AT GENUS `0`, A DEGREE-ZERO PICARD CLASS IS TRIVIAL
13	
14	The degree homomorphism `classDeg` (`RiemannRoch/Degree.lean`) has a large landed API in one
15	direction — `classDeg_one`, `classDeg_mul`, `classDeg_inv`, `classDeg_picClass`,
16	`classDeg_eq_zero_of_mem_picFromBase` — every one of which computes a degree *from* a class.
17	**The converse is absent**: nothing in the tree concludes that a class is trivial from its
18	degree, at any genus.  A name census cannot see that gap, because the missing statement has
19	no name; what shows it is that the degree-zero *subgroup* has 93 consumers and no producer.
20	
21	This file supplies the converse at `χ(𝒪) = 1`, i.e. at genus `0`.
22	
23	## The argument
24	
25	Three landed steps, no new mathematics:
26	
27	1. every Čech class is the class of a Weil divisor
28	   (`Scheme.CurveDivisor.exists_picClass_eq`), and the degrees agree (`classDeg_picClass`);
29	2. the χ-ledger `χ(𝒪(D)) = χ(𝒪) + deg D` (`chi_divisorSheaf`) at `deg D = 0` and `χ(𝒪) = 1`
30	   gives `χ(𝒪(D)) = 1`, hence `h⁰ > 0` since `χ = h⁰ - h¹` and `h¹ ≥ 0`.  **This is where
31	   genus `0` enters, and it is the only place**;
32	3. `exists_effective_of_h0_pos` turns the section into an *effective* representative of the
33	   same class, whose degree is therefore still `0`; and an effective divisor of degree `≤ 0`
34	   is `0` (`Scheme.CurveDivisor.eq_zero_of_deg_le_zero`, coefficients nonnegative weighted by
35	   positive residue degrees).  So the class is the class of `0`, which is `1`.
36	
37	**No `H¹`-vanishing hypothesis is needed.**  χ alone forces the section: `h⁰ = χ + h¹ ≥ χ`.
38	That is worth stating explicitly because every other section-producing consumer in the tree
39	carries a `Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule … 1)` binder for the divisor sheaf, and here it would
40	be dead weight — the binder is about `𝒪(D)`, whose `h¹` the argument never needs to know.
41	
42	## What this is for
43	
44	It is the field-level layer of the degree-zero Picard vanishing that
45	`Picard/Pic0VanishingAffineReduction.lean` reduces to test rings, and the debt
46	`Albanese/Genus0Terminal.lean` isolates.  It does **not** discharge that debt: the vanishing
47	quantifies over test *rings*, and this statement is over a *field*.  The remaining step is the
48	ring-level one, and it is not supplied here.
49	
50	## Main declarations
51	
52	* `AlgebraicGeometry.eq_one_of_classDeg_eq_zero_of_chi_one` — **the converse of the degree
53	  API**: at `χ(𝒪) = 1`, a Čech Picard class of degree `0` is trivial.
54	* `AlgebraicGeometry.classDeg_eq_zero_iff_eq_one_of_chi_one` — bundled as an iff with the
55	  landed `classDeg_one`, so both directions sit under one name.
56	-/

74	
75	The direction the tree's degree API was missing.  Genus `0` enters exactly once: through the
76	χ-ledger, which at `deg D = 0` and `χ(𝒪) = 1` gives `χ(𝒪(D)) = 1` and hence a global section.

78	degree `0` and is therefore the zero divisor.

12	
13	`Picard/Pic0VanishingAffineReduction.lean` reduces the `∀ T` binder of the degree-zero Picard

15	of that statement at genus `0`, for an arbitrary base field and every field extension.

21	## Why the base change is the whole plumbing cost
22	
23	`relPicDeg L` is a homomorphism out of `relPic C (overSpec k L)`, whose representatives are
24	Čech classes on `(C ⊗ overSpec k L).left` — the curve base-changed to `L`, *not* `C`.  So the
25	`χ = 1` hypothesis has to hold at the base-changed curve at **every** field extension, and
26	`genus C = 0` is a statement about `C` over `k`.
27	
28	That transport is landed and needs no new cohomology: `finrank_h0_baseField` and
29	`finrank_h1_baseField_eq_genus` (`Cohomology/H1BaseFieldInvariance.lean:353,363`) compute both
30	Betti numbers of the base-changed curve, and `h0_moduleKSheaf` gives `h⁰ = 1` over `k`.  Then
31	`χ = h⁰ - h¹ = 1 - genus C = 1`.

34	`(C ⊗ overSpec k L).left.moduleKSheaf L` under `instOverBaseChange`
35	(`Curve/BaseChangeInstances.lean:74`), which is the key `relPicDeg`'s degree stack consumes.

37	*same object* under a different `Over` instance, and the resulting `chi` terms do not unify —
38	measured, so the identities are used directly rather than the bundled χ lemma.

42	* **It is not the vanishing.**  After the affine reduction the surviving obligation quantifies
43	  over test *rings*; a field is a ring, so this is one instance of it and not the statement.
44	  The general-ring case needs a fibrewise-to-global argument (cohomology and base change) that
45	  this tree does not have, and nothing here supplies it.
46	* **It says nothing at positive genus**, and it does not claim to: at `genus C > 0` the
47	  hypothesis `genus C = 0` simply fails, and this file exhibits no positive-genus curve.
48	* **It does not produce a `JacobianData`** on its own.  The producer
49	  `jacobianData_of_overSpec_subsingleton` wants the ring-level hypothesis; the field case does
50	  not discharge it.

55	  base-changed curve, at every field extension, from `genus C = 0`.

14	vanishing is *equivalent* to the same statement at affine tests `overSpec k A`.  This file

20	`Pic0VanishingRoute.jacobianData_of_subsingleton` turns into a `JacobianData` and which
21	`Pic0ChartSeamPairDecided.isLocallySurjective_abelSigmaChartZero_iff` shows *is* the seam's
22	coverage antecedent at parameter `0` — therefore now has all of its field instances closed on
23	a genus-`0` curve, and only its **ring** instances open.
24	
25	## The two steps, and what each costs
26	
27	**Step 1, through the plus construction** (`eq_one_of_degAff_eq_zero_of_genus_zero`).  A plus
28	class of `PicEtAff C K` is `mk E x` for some étale cover `E` of `K`; its degree is by
29	definition read on a finite separable *field* refinement of `E`
30	(`PicEtAff.degAff_mk`), and `Pic0VanishingFieldGenusZero` kills the transported class there.
31	Transport back is free: `PicEtAff.mk_descentMap` says the plus class does not change along a
32	refinement, and `PicEtAff.mk_one` closes it.
33	
34	Note what is *not* needed: **no surjectivity of the plus unit**.  The landed
35	`PicEtAff.unit_surjective_of_section` (`EffectivityClose.lean:141`) requires a curve section
36	over the test field, which this project constructs nowhere; the argument here never asks
37	whether the class comes from `relPic C (overSpec k K)` itself, only what happens on its own
38	cover carrier.  So the field case needs no rational point.
39	
40	**Step 2, off the degree condition** (`subsingleton_pic0Subgroup_overSpec_field_of_genus_zero`).
41	Membership in `pic0Subgroup` quantifies over *all* field points of the test; at an affine test
42	over a field, the identity `𝟙 (overSpec k K)` is one of them, and `degAt` at the identity is
43	`degAff` of the class by `picEtMap_id`.  So a single instantiation of the membership binder
44	supplies the hypothesis of step 1 — the other field points are not consulted.
45	
46	## What remains, stated exactly
47	
48	  `∀ (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [Algebra k A], Subsingleton (pic0Subgroup C (overSpec k A))`
49	
50	for `A` **not** a field.  That is fibrewise-degree-zero implies globally trivial over a base
51	ring, i.e. cohomology and base change; nothing in this tree proves it, and it is the whole
52	remaining distance from here to a `JacobianData` at a genus-`0` curve via
53	`jacobianData_of_overSpec_subsingleton`.
54	
55	Two things this does **not** do, to forestall the obvious misreadings:
56	
57	* it does not compute `Pic(ℙ¹)` or any Picard group — degree-zero classes are killed without
58	  identifying the group they sit in;
59	* it says nothing at positive genus, and exhibits no positive-genus curve.
60	
61	## Main declarations

63	* `AlgebraicGeometry.eq_one_of_degAff_eq_zero_of_genus_zero` — a plus class of degree `0` over
64	  a field test is trivial, at genus `0`.  Needs no curve section.
65	* `AlgebraicGeometry.subsingleton_pic0Subgroup_overSpec_field_of_genus_zero` — **the field-test
66	  vanishing**.

68	  curve**: the same at `P1.asOver k` with *no hypothesis at all*, since
69	  `Curve/P1H1Vanishing.lean` supplies `genus (P1.asOver k) = 0` over an arbitrary field.

72	(measured — the linter reports it), even though the surrounding `picEt` descent material
73	carries four.

92	/-- **A plus class of degree zero over a field test is trivial, at genus `0`.**

94	`degAff` is *defined* by reading the relative degree on a finite separable field refinement of
95	the class's own cover (`PicEtAff.degAff_mk`), which is exactly where the field layer
96	`relPic_eq_one_of_relPicDeg_eq_zero_of_genus_zero` applies.  Transport back to the original

100	surjectivity `PicEtAff.unit_surjective_of_section` is not used, because the argument works on
101	the representative's own cover carrier rather than asking the class to come from `relPic`. -/
102	theorem eq_one_of_degAff_eq_zero_of_genus_zero
103	    (K : Type u) [Field K] [Algebra k K] (hg : genus C = 0)
104	    (q : PicEtAff C K) (hq : PicEtAff.degAff (C := C) K q = 0) : q = 1 := by
105	  induction q using PicEtAff.ind with
106	  | mk E x =>
107	    obtain ⟨L, hLf, hLa, hLfin, hLsep, ⟨j⟩⟩ := E.exists_finiteSeparableField_algHom

117	        (x : relPic C (overSpec k E.Carrier)) = 1 :=

119	    -- transport to the field cover does not change the plus class

123	    rw [← hstep]

125	    refine Subtype.ext ?_
126	    rw [descentMap_coe]
127	    have hcomp :
128	        ((Algebra.EtaleCover.ofFieldEquiv (K := K) L).symm.toAlgHom.comp j).restrictScalars k
129	          = ((Algebra.EtaleCover.ofFieldEquiv (K := K) L).symm.toAlgHom.restrictScalars k).comp
130	            (j.restrictScalars k) := rfl
131	    rw [hcomp, relPicAlgMap_comp, htriv, map_one]
132	    rfl

134	set_option maxHeartbeats 1600000 in
135	-- Same instance stack, plus the affine comparison.
136	omit [GeometricallyReduced C.hom] in
137	/-- **THE FIELD-TEST VANISHING**: at `genus C = 0`, the degree-zero Picard group of the curve
138	vanishes at every affine test over a *field*.
139	
140	Only **one** field point of the test is consulted — the identity `𝟙 (overSpec k K)`, at which
141	`degAt` is `degAff` of the class by `picEtMap_id`.  So the `∀ K, ∀ t` binder of
142	`pic0Subgroup`'s membership is used at a single instantiation, and the remaining field points
143	carry no weight in this direction. -/
144	theorem subsingleton_pic0Subgroup_overSpec_field_of_genus_zero
145	    (K : Type u) [Field K] [Algebra k K] (hg : genus C = 0) :
146	    Subsingleton (pic0Subgroup C (overSpec k K)) := by
147	  refine ⟨fun s t => Subtype.ext ?_⟩
148	  refine (picEtAffineEquiv C K).injective ?_
149	  have hs : PicEtAff.degAff (C := C) K (picEtAffineEquiv C K s.1) = 0 := by
150	    have h := s.2 K (𝟙 (overSpec k K))
151	    rwa [degAt, picEtMap_id] at h
152	  have ht : PicEtAff.degAff (C := C) K (picEtAffineEquiv C K t.1) = 0 := by
153	    have h := t.2 K (𝟙 (overSpec k K))
154	    rwa [degAt, picEtMap_id] at h
155	  have h1 := eq_one_of_degAff_eq_zero_of_genus_zero C K hg (picEtAffineEquiv C K s.1) hs
156	  have h2 := eq_one_of_degAff_eq_zero_of_genus_zero C K hg (picEtAffineEquiv C K t.1) ht
157	  exact h1.trans h2.symm
158	
159	/-! ## Non-vacuity: the statement fires at a curve, unconditionally -/
160	
161	/-- **The field-test vanishing at `ℙ¹`, with no hypothesis.**
162	
163	`Curve/P1Curve.lean` gives `P1.asOver k` the three curve binders over an arbitrary field and

168	    (k : Type u) [Field k] (K : Type u) [Field K] [Algebra k K] :

170	  subsingleton_pic0Subgroup_overSpec_field_of_genus_zero (P1.asOver k) K

/-!
# The relative Picard functor of a curve

For a scheme `C` over a field `k` (an object of `Over (Spec k)`) this file defines the
relative Picard functor of Grothendieck–Kleiman:
$$\operatorname{Pic}_{C/k}(T) \;=\; \operatorname{Pic}(C \times_k T)\,/\,
  \operatorname{Pic}(T),$$
line-bundle classes on `C ⊗ T` modulo classes pulled back from the test object `T`
along the second projection. The quotient — never the absolute `Pic(C ⊗ T)`, which is
not even a separated presheaf in any useful sense — is the functor that étale
sheafification and the representability theorem consume.

Products are the cartesian-monoidal product of `Over (Spec k)` (chosen pullbacks of
schemes): `C ⊗ T`, projection `snd C T`, whiskering `C ◁ g`, matching the vocabulary
of the challenge statement file.

## Main declarations

* `AlgebraicGeometry.picFromBase C T`: the subgroup of `(C ⊗ T).left.CechPic` of classes
  pulled back from `T` along the second projection.
* `AlgebraicGeometry.relPic C T`: the relative Picard group, the quotient by
  `picFromBase C T`, a `CommGroup`; `relPicMk` is the projection, with
  `relPicMk_eq_relPicMk_iff` the exact coset relation (a genuine range condition, no
  choice, no `Nonempty (≅)`).
* `AlgebraicGeometry.relPicMap C g`: restriction along `g : T' ⟶ T`, descended from
  pullback of Čech classes along `C ◁ g`.
* `AlgebraicGeometry.relPicFunctor C`: the relative Picard functor
  `(Over (Spec k))ᵒᵖ ⥤ CommGrpCat`.
-/

set_option autoImplicit false

universe u

open CategoryTheory Limits MonoidalCategory CartesianMonoidalCategory Opposite
open AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme (CechPic)

namespace AlgebraicGeometry

variable {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))

noncomputable section

/-- The subgroup of Picard classes on `C ⊗ T` pulled back from the test object `T`
along the second projection. The relative Picard group is the quotient by it. -/
def picFromBase (T : Over (Spec (.of k))) : Subgroup ((C ⊗ T).left.CechPic) :=
  (CechPic.map (snd C T).left).range

lemma mem_picFromBase_iff {T : Over (Spec (.of k))} {L : (C ⊗ T).left.CechPic} :
    L ∈ picFromBase C T ↔ ∃ N : T.left.CechPic, CechPic.map (snd C T).left N = L :=
  Iff.rfl

/-- The relative Picard group of `C/k` at a test object `T`: Picard classes on `C ⊗ T`
modulo classes pulled back from `T`. -/
def relPic (T : Over (Spec (.of k))) : Type u :=
  (C ⊗ T).left.CechPic ⧸ picFromBase C T

noncomputable instance (T : Over (Spec (.of k))) : CommGroup (relPic C T) :=
  QuotientGroup.Quotient.commGroup (picFromBase C T)

/-- The projection from Picard classes on `C ⊗ T` to the relative Picard group. -/
noncomputable def relPicMk (T : Over (Spec (.of k))) :
    (C ⊗ T).left.CechPic →* relPic C T :=
  QuotientGroup.mk' (picFromBase C T)

lemma relPicMk_surjective (T : Over (Spec (.of k))) :
    Function.Surjective (relPicMk C T) :=
  QuotientGroup.mk'_surjective (picFromBase C T)

/-- The exact coset relation: two Picard classes on `C ⊗ T` have equal image in the
relative Picard group iff their ratio is pulled back from `T`. -/
lemma relPicMk_eq_relPicMk_iff {T : Over (Spec (.of k))}
    {L L' : (C ⊗ T).left.CechPic} :
    relPicMk C T L = relPicMk C T L' ↔ L / L' ∈ picFromBase C T :=
  QuotientGroup.eq_iff_div_mem

@[elab_as_elim]
theorem relPic.ind {T : Over (Spec (.of k))} {motive : relPic C T → Prop}
    (mk : ∀ L : (C ⊗ T).left.CechPic, motive (relPicMk C T L)) (x : relPic C T) :
    motive x :=
  QuotientGroup.induction_on x mk

/-- Pullback of Čech Picard classes along `C ◁ g` sends classes from `T` to classes
from `T'`: the well-definedness of `relPicMap` on the `H_T`-cosets. -/
lemma picFromBase_le_comap (g : T' ⟶ T) :

  rintro _ ⟨N, rfl⟩
  refine ⟨CechPic.map g.left N, ?_⟩
  show CechPic.map (snd C T').left (CechPic.map g.left N)

  rw [← MonoidHom.comp_apply, ← MonoidHom.comp_apply, ← Scheme.CechPic.map_comp,

  QuotientGroup.map (picFromBase C T) (picFromBase C T')
    (CechPic.map (C ◁ g).left) (picFromBase_le_comap C g)

@[simp]
lemma relPicMap_mk (g : T' ⟶ T) (L : (C ⊗ T).left.CechPic) :
    relPicMap C g (relPicMk C T L) = relPicMk C T' (CechPic.map (C ◁ g).left L) :=
  QuotientGroup.map_mk' _ _ _ _ L

lemma relPicMap_id (x : relPic C T) : relPicMap C (𝟙 T) x = x := by
  induction x using relPic.ind with
  | mk L =>
    rw [relPicMap_mk, MonoidalCategory.whiskerLeft_id, Over.id_left,
      Scheme.CechPic.map_id]
    rfl

import AlgebraicJacobian.Curve.P1DegreeZeroTrivial
import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.Pic0VanishingAffineReduction

/-!
# `Pic⁰(ℙ¹)` VANISHES AT EVERY FIELD TEST — the first producer of the hypothesis at a curve

`hvan : ∀ T, Subsingleton (pic0Subgroup C T)` is where both live routes to a `rep` producer
meet, and it has had **no producer at any curve**.  This file supplies it at `ℙ¹` for every
test of the form `overSpec k K` with `K/k` a field extension:

  `Subsingleton (pic0Subgroup (P1.asOver k) (overSpec k K))`.

That is a genuine instance of the hypothesis, not a reformulation of it: nothing here assumes
a vanishing, a chart atlas, a coverage clause, a divisor representability, or a rational point.

## Why the field case is not the fibrewise case

`Curve/P1DegreeZeroTrivial.lean` proves that a Čech Picard class on `ℙ¹_K` of degree `0` is
trivial.  That is a statement about `CechPic`, and `pic0Subgroup` is three constructions above
it: `pic0Subgroup C T ≤ picEt C T`, `picEt C T` is a compatible family of `PicEtAff C Γ(T,U)`
over the affine opens of `T`, and `PicEtAff C A` is the one-step étale **plus** of
`relPic C (overSpec k A)`, itself a quotient of `CechPic ((C ⊗ overSpec k A).left)`.  Getting
from the bottom to the top is the content below, and each of the three steps is a real one.

## The three steps

1. **`relPic`** (`relPic_eq_one_of_relPicDeg_eq_zero`).  `relPic` is `CechPic` modulo classes
   pulled back from the base, so a class is `relPicMk L`; `relPicDeg` of it is `classDeg L` by
   the anchor, and the degree-zero triviality applies to `L` itself.

2. **`PicEtAff`** (`picEtAff_eq_one_of_degAff_eq_zero`), the step with actual content.  A plus
   class is represented on an *étale cover* `E`, not on a field, and `relPic` triviality is
   only available over fields.  The bridge is that field covers are **cofinal**
   (`Algebra.EtaleCover.exists_finiteSeparableField_algHom`): refine `E` into a finite
   separable field extension `L/K`, where `degAff_mk` says the degree is `relPicDeg L` of the
   transported representative.  Step 1 at `L` kills it, and `mk_descentMap` says the plus class
   computed on the refinement is the same class.

   One detail worth recording because it removes an obligation: the transport is pushed
   **forward** along the inverse of the carrier identification `ofFieldEquiv`, so no
   injectivity of `relPicAlgMap` is needed — and the tree proves none.

3. **`pic0Subgroup`** (`subsingleton_pic0Subgroup_overSpec`).  At `T = overSpec k K` the
   membership condition is quantified over *all* field points of `T`, and the identity
   `𝟙 (overSpec k K)` **is** one of them.  So the hypothesis, instantiated at the identity,
   gives exactly `degAff = 0` for the plus class through `picEtAffineEquiv` — the degree
   condition at a single well-chosen point is the whole of what step 2 consumes.

## What remains, stated exactly

`jacobianData_of_overSpec_subsingleton` (`Pic0VanishingAffineReduction.lean:266`) needs the
same statement at every commutative `k`-**algebra** `A`, not only at fields, and that is *not*
what this file proves.  The surviving gap is therefore sharp and singular:

  `∀ (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [Algebra k A],`
  `  Subsingleton (pic0Subgroup (P1.asOver k) (overSpec k A))`

and its content is `Pic(ℙ¹_A) ≅ Pic(A) × ℤ` — cohomology and base change.  Two routes are
**foreclosed** rather than merely unattempted, and both were priced before this file:

* the chart route does not extend, because chart triviality over `A` requires
  `Pic(A[t]) = Pic(A)`, i.e. Traverso's theorem, true exactly for **seminormal** `A` — false in
  general, and mathlib contains no seminormality at all;
* the `picEt`-level reduction `subsingleton_pic0_of_affine` (`Pic0VanishingRoute.lean:283`)
  runs one way and its hypothesis is vanishing of the *whole* `picEt`, which is false at `ℙ¹`
  since a degree-one class exists there.

What this file does buy toward the ring case is that the degree machinery is now known to be
*sharp* at this curve over every field: any counterexample over a ring cannot come from a
fibre.

## Main declarations

* `AlgebraicGeometry.P1.relPic_eq_one_of_relPicDeg_eq_zero` — step 1.
* `AlgebraicGeometry.P1.picEtAff_eq_one_of_degAff_eq_zero` — step 2, through cofinal field
  covers.
* `AlgebraicGeometry.P1.subsingleton_pic0Subgroup_overSpec` — **the producer**: `Pic⁰(ℙ¹)`
  vanishes at every field test.
* `AlgebraicGeometry.P1.pic0Subgroup_overSpec_eq_bot` — the `= ⊥` spelling, which is the one
  `Albanese/Genus0Terminal.lean` consumes.
-/

variable (k : Type u) [Field k] (K : Type u) [Field K] [Algebra k K]

/-! ## Step 1: the relative Picard group over a field -/

/-- **A degree-zero relative Picard class of `ℙ¹` over a field extension is trivial.**

`relPic` is `CechPic` modulo the classes pulled back from the base, and `relPicDeg` is
`classDeg` on a representative (`relPicDeg_relPicMk`), so this is
`eq_one_of_classDeg_eq_zero_baseChange` composed with the quotient map. -/
theorem relPic_eq_one_of_relPicDeg_eq_zero
    (x : relPic (P1.asOver k) (overSpec k K)) (hx : relPicDeg K x = 0) : x = 1 := by
  induction x using relPic.ind with
  | mk L =>
    rw [relPicDeg_relPicMk] at hx
    rw [eq_one_of_classDeg_eq_zero_baseChange k K L hx]
    exact map_one _

/-! ## Step 2: the étale plus construction, through cofinal field covers -/

/-- **A degree-zero plus class of `ℙ¹` at a field is trivial.**

The step that is not formal.  A plus class lives on an étale cover `E` of `K`, where step 1 is
unavailable — `relPic` triviality needs a *field*.  Field covers are cofinal, so refine `E`
into a finite separable extension `L/K`; there `degAff_mk` computes the degree as `relPicDeg L`
of the transported representative, step 1 applies, and `mk_descentMap` identifies the plus class
computed on the refinement with the original.

The transport is pushed forward along `ofFieldEquiv.symm` rather than reflected back, so no
injectivity of `relPicAlgMap` is required (the tree proves none). -/
theorem picEtAff_eq_one_of_degAff_eq_zero
    (z : PicEtAff (P1.asOver k) K) (hz : PicEtAff.degAff K z = 0) : z = 1 := by
  induction z using PicEtAff.ind with
  | _ E x =>
    obtain ⟨L, _, _, _, _, ⟨j⟩⟩ := E.exists_finiteSeparableField_algHom
    letI : Algebra k L := ((algebraMap K L).comp (algebraMap k K)).toAlgebra
    haveI : IsScalarTower k K L := .of_algebraMap_eq fun _ => rfl
    -- the field cover of `L`, whose carrier is `L` itself
    set F : Algebra.EtaleCover K := Algebra.EtaleCover.ofField (K := K) L with hF
    set jF : E.Carrier →ₐ[K] F.Carrier :=
      (Algebra.EtaleCover.ofFieldEquiv (K := K) L).symm.toAlgHom.comp j with hjF
    have hdeg := PicEtAff.degAff_mk (C := P1.asOver k) (K := K) E x L j
    rw [hz] at hdeg
    rw [← PicEtAff.mk_descentMap (C := P1.asOver k) jF x]
    have h1 : relPicAlgMap (P1.asOver k) (AlgHom.restrictScalars k j)
        (x : relPic (P1.asOver k) (overSpec k E.Carrier)) = 1 :=
      relPic_eq_one_of_relPicDeg_eq_zero k L _ hdeg.symm
    -- push forward along the inverse carrier identification
    have h2 := congrArg (relPicAlgMap (P1.asOver k)
      ((Algebra.EtaleCover.ofFieldEquiv (K := K) L).symm.toAlgHom.restrictScalars k)) h1
    rw [map_one, ← relPicAlgMap_comp] at h2
    have hcomp :
        ((Algebra.EtaleCover.ofFieldEquiv (K := K) L).symm.toAlgHom.restrictScalars k).comp
          (AlgHom.restrictScalars k j) = AlgHom.restrictScalars k jF := rfl
    rw [hcomp] at h2
    have hone : descentMap (P1.asOver k) jF x = 1 := by
      apply Subtype.ext
      show (descentMap (P1.asOver k) jF x : relPic (P1.asOver k) (overSpec k F.Carrier))
        = ((1 : descentClasses (P1.asOver k) F) : relPic (P1.asOver k) (overSpec k F.Carrier))
      rw [descentMap_coe]
      exact h2
    rw [hone]
    exact PicEtAff.mk_one _ _

/-! ## Step 3: the producer -/

/-- **`Pic⁰(ℙ¹)` vanishes at every field test.**  The first producer of the `hvan` hypothesis
at any curve in this project.

The degree-zero condition is quantified over all field points of the test, and at
`T = overSpec k K` the **identity** is one of them.  Instantiating there and transporting
through the affine comparison `picEtAffineEquiv` gives exactly the `degAff = 0` that step 2
consumes.  So the single well-chosen point carries the whole hypothesis; no cover, no gluing,
and no naturality is used. -/
theorem subsingleton_pic0Subgroup_overSpec :
    Subsingleton (pic0Subgroup (P1.asOver k) (overSpec k K)) := by
  refine ⟨fun s t => Subtype.ext ?_⟩
  refine (picEtAffineEquiv (P1.asOver k) K).injective ?_
  have hs : PicEtAff.degAff K (picEtAffineEquiv (P1.asOver k) K s.1) = 0 := by
    have hid := s.2 K (𝟙 (overSpec k K))
    rw [degAt, picEtMap_id] at hid
    exact hid
  have ht : PicEtAff.degAff K (picEtAffineEquiv (P1.asOver k) K t.1) = 0 := by
    have hid := t.2 K (𝟙 (overSpec k K))
    rw [degAt, picEtMap_id] at hid
    exact hid
  rw [picEtAff_eq_one_of_degAff_eq_zero k K _ hs, picEtAff_eq_one_of_degAff_eq_zero k K _ ht]

/-- The `= ⊥` spelling, which is the form `Albanese/Genus0Terminal.lean` consumes. -/
theorem pic0Subgroup_overSpec_eq_bot :
    pic0Subgroup (P1.asOver k) (overSpec k K) = ⊥ :=
  pic0Subgroup_eq_bot_of_subsingleton (subsingleton_pic0Subgroup_overSpec k K)

This is the **shared plus-class collapse lemma** flagged by `w4-datb-worksheet.md` §5
risk 6 and by the B-4 landing note I-0252 ("state it once as a named lemma with a
characterizing property … both consume it"): a plus class of the one-step étale-plus

suitable finite separable field extension.

Over a field `K`, a plus class `p : PicEtAff C K` is `PicEtAff.mk E x` for a presented
étale cover `E` of `Spec K` and a descent class `x` (`Picard/PicEtAff.lean`).  Field
cofinality (`Algebra.EtaleCover.exists_finiteSeparableField_algHom`,
`Algebra/EtaleCover.lean` — étale covers of a field are refined by finite separable field
extensions) supplies a finite separable `L/K` together with a `K`-algebra map
`ℓ : E.Carrier →ₐ[K] L`.  Base-changing `E` to `L` yields a cover with an `L`-point, so the
base-changed descent class is, by the descent/cocycle condition (`relPicAlgMap_congr`), the
tautological datum of an honest class: `PicEtAff.map C L p` is the plus-unit of the
relative-Picard class `relPicAlgMap ℓ x` on `C_L` (`PicEtAff.unit C L …`).

* `AlgebraicGeometry.PicEtAff.map_mk_eq_unit_of_algHom` — the collapse: `mk C E x`

(`Algebra.EtaleCover.exists_finiteSeparableField_algHom`).  Both statements take the tower

24	So the field-point content of the vanishing is a statement about `ℙ¹_K` for every `K`, and a
25	computation over `k` alone does not touch it.

28	
29	`genus (baseChangeBundle C K) = genus C` is base-field invariance of the genus
